Question: Is the “ability to consummate” concept subject to Material Adverse Change carveouts?
Option A: No
Option B: Yes

Merger Agreement: “Material Adverse Change” means any event, change, condition or circumstance that (i) causes a material deterioration in the overall financial condition or operating performance of the Company and its Subsidiaries, or (ii) directly prevents or substantially delays the Company’s ability to complete its merger transaction by the specified deadline. Notwithstanding the foregoing, for the purposes of clause (i), adverse effects which result solely from broad economic downturns, nationwide regulatory modifications, or industry-wide market volatility shall not be considered in assessing a Material Adverse Change. However, with respect to clause (ii), no similar exclusions or exceptions are provided; any delay or impairment directly affecting the consummation of the merger—including those due to isolated operational failures or targeted regulatory/legal challenges—will be fully taken into account in determining a Material Adverse Change. 

Based on the above provisions, assess whether the carveout provisions apply to the ability to consummate.

Question: Is the “ability to consummate” concept subject to Material Adverse Effect (MAE) carveouts?
Option A: No
Option B: Yes

Merger Agreement: “Total Material Adverse Impact” means any event, change, occurrence or effect that, whether occurring individually or in combination with other effects, (i) has produced or is reasonably expected to produce a material adverse effect on the business, financial condition, or operations of the Company; and (ii) would prevent, materially delay, or otherwise impair the Company’s ability to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement. Notwithstanding any provisions elsewhere, for the purposes of clause (ii) concerning the ability to consummate, no carveout or exclusion shall apply—even if the event arises from general economic downturns, changes in accounting principles, shifts in credit or capital market conditions, or other factors normally excluded under standard MAE definitions. Conversely, adverse effects described solely under clause (i) may be subject to standard carveouts as detailed in Section 4.3.
